label: TP
reason: Both alerts are valid. Alert 1 (XSS): User input from header flows through doSomething() -> bar -> sql -> encodeForHTML() -> response.getWriter(). While encodeForHTML() mitigates XSS in the response output, the SQL injection vulnerability at line 56 remains exploitable. Alert 2 (SQL Injection): User input from header flows through doSomething() -> bar -> sql at line 56, concatenated directly into SQL query without parameterization before DatabaseHelper.JDBCtemplate.execute(). The resolved sink value 'bar' depends on attacker-controlled header input.

evidence.note: User input from header flows through param -> doSomething() -> bar, with list manipulation that preserves user data at index 1
SQL query at L56 uses bar (tainted) without parameterization; XSS output at L59-62 is HTML-encoded
